# GitLab Connection Requirements Checklist: Security and API

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of credential-security and connection-validation requirements.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are credential creation, replacement, preservation, and explicit removal requirements distinguishable as separate lifecycle outcomes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–004, §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the credential status fields and meanings fully specified without requiring any masked or partial token representation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, §FR-013–014]
- [ ] CHK003 Are status retrieval, credential writing/removal, persisted-token validation, and candidate-token validation all covered by explicit contract requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009–010, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK004 Are credential persistence and configuration retirement requirements clear about preserving Monitoring Configuration data while making the credential unavailable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-022]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the distinction between an empty token during an unrelated configuration update and an empty token during an explicit credential replacement unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002–003, §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the five user-facing connection states clearly differentiated, including which states describe persisted metadata versus a temporary validation in progress? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the specification clearly limit successful validation to reachability, authentication, and basic authenticated API access without implying readiness for Feature 004 discovery? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the user-visible meanings of invalid credentials, forbidden access, unreachable instance, timeout, and unexpected response clear and non-sensitive? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Are the rules for a failed candidate-token validation consistent with the rules for a failed validation of the persisted credential? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK010 Are credential replacement and GitLab URL changes consistently specified to invalidate prior validation success without changing unrelated configuration values? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK011 Are validation result state and last-successful-validation time defined consistently when a later validation fails? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, User Story 2 Scenario 9]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the requirements clear that credential actions never enable/disable a configuration or initiate discovery/mining? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017–018, §FR-024, §FR-026]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 Can the success criteria objectively distinguish credential secrecy, encrypted persistence, validation outcome, and UI state coverage? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-002–005]
- [ ] CHK014 Do the acceptance criteria explicitly cover retention of the prior successful-validation time after a failed revalidation while showing the latest failure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, §FR-014]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Are the effects of a failed credential replacement specified, including whether the prior credential remains usable when persistence fails? [Gap, Spec §FR-002–003, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are repeated or concurrent save, replace, remove, and validation requests covered with clear conflict and preservation outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK017 Are outcomes defined when the configuration is retired or becomes unavailable while credential storage or validation is in progress? [Coverage, Spec §FR-022, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the differences between removing a credential and retiring its Monitoring Configuration explicit for retained validation metadata? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-022, Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK019 Do security requirements cover raw and decrypted tokens, encryption keys, encrypted values, authorization headers, logs, telemetry, API responses, and browser storage? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006–008, §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK020 Are encryption-configuration failure and key-loss outcomes clearly distinguished so failures cannot be mistaken for an unconfigured credential? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK021 Are timeout and unavailable-instance expectations defined sufficiently for user feedback without implying unsupported performance guarantees? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Assumptions]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK022 Is the required compatibility behavior for supported GitLab instances clear enough to interpret a basic authenticated API validation result? [Assumption, Spec §FR-011, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK023 Are permissions required for future discovery explicitly assigned to Feature 004 rather than implied by this feature's successful validation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024, Scope Boundaries]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK024 Do the credential-preservation requirements avoid conflict between blank-input semantics and explicit credential removal? [Conflict, Spec §FR-003–004, §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK025 Is it explicit whether last-success metadata is retained only after a failed revalidation of the same credential, but invalidated on credential replacement, URL change, or removal? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014–016, User Story 2 Scenario 9]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
